objects.description: Standard library pair used to hold a single HTTP-style header key and value as string_views. It is referenced as a parameter type for getHeaders but not defined here; included for completeness note: this is not custom to this header and should be ignored per instructions.
Parses semicolon- and equals-delimited parameter strings (such as Content-Disposition header parameters) and yields successive key/value pairs. Handles optional quoting and whitespace trimming.

Parses HTTP multipart bodies using a boundary extracted from a Content-Type value. After setBody, iterates parts with getNextPart, returning each part body and filling headers via an external getHeaders function (declared elsewhere). Not re-iterable because the parser mutates the buffer by padding a trailing CR.

Iterator-like helper for parsing HTTP chunked transfer-encoded payloads using getNextChunk. Holds pointers to input data (std::string_view) and parser state (uint64_t) and yields successive data chunks (excluding CRLF) as std::string_view until exhaustion. Supports optional trailer-dropping behavior via the trailer flag. Construction requires the caller to provide references to the data buffer and state storage that outlive the iterator. No ownership; non-copy-eliding begin/end pattern for range-style loops. Increment advances by parsing next chunk; dereference returns current chunk or aborts if invalid.

functions.name: uWS::utils::u32toaHex
functions.description: Converts an unsigned 32-bit integer to its lowercase hexadecimal representation (without 0x prefix) and writes the digits contiguously to dst. Returns the number of characters written. The output is not null-terminated. Typical usage: provide a buffer of at least 8 bytes (plus one more byte if you intend to add a null terminator yourself), call the function, then optionally append '\0' using the returned length.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable, non-null pointer.

dst must have enough capacity for the hexadecimal digits of value; in the worst case (value = 0xffffffff) this is 8 characters. Allocate at least 8 bytes, or 9 if you intend to add a null-terminator yourself.
The function does not write a null-terminator; callers must append one if a C-string is required.
value is treated as an unsigned 32-bit integer; negative values are not applicable.
Thread-safe as it uses no shared state; dst must not alias read-only memory.

functions.name: uWS::utils::u64toa
functions.description: Converts an unsigned 64-bit integer to its decimal representation and writes the digits contiguously to dst. Returns the number of characters written. The output is not null-terminated. Typical usage: provide a buffer of up to 20 bytes (plus one more byte if you intend to add a null terminator), call the function, then optionally append '\0' using the returned length.
requirements: dst must be a valid, writable, non-null pointer.

dst must have enough capacity for the decimal digits of value; in the worst case (value = 18446744073709551615) this is 20 characters. Allocate at least 20 bytes, or 21 if you intend to add a null-terminator yourself.
The function does not write a null-terminator; callers must append one if a C-string is required.
value is treated as an unsigned 64-bit integer; negative values are not applicable.
Thread-safe as it uses no shared state; dst must not alias read-only memory.

functions.name: uWS::getHeaders
functions.signature: static inline unsigned int uWS::getHeaders(char *postPaddedBuffer, char *end, std::pair<std::string_view, std::string_view> *headers)
functions.description: Parses RFC 822–style header lines from a mutable buffer and populates an array of (key, value) string_views. Keys are lowercased in-place while scanning. Stops at the empty line (CRLF) that terminates the header section and returns the number of bytes consumed from the start of the buffer up to and including that terminating CRLF. Returns 0 on parse failure (malformed header line, missing CRLFs, or exceeding the header limit). Intended for HTTP and multipart parsing where at most MAX_HEADERS (10) headers are accepted. The produced string_views alias the input buffer; the buffer must remain valid for the lifetime of those views.
requirements: postPaddedBuffer must point to the beginning of a writable, contiguous char buffer containing only the header section to parse.
end must point to one-past-the-last byte that may be examined; end >= postPaddedBuffer.
The buffer must contain properly formatted header lines terminated by "\r\n" and a final empty line "\r\n" within [postPaddedBuffer, end).

Because the function checks postPaddedBuffer[1] after encountering a '\r', the buffer must provide the following '\n' byte within bounds; reading beyond end is not guarded here. Ensure CRLF pairs are fully within [postPaddedBuffer, end).
Header field names are lowercased in-place (bytes before the ':'); the input buffer must be mutable and may not be reused elsewhere expecting original casing.
headers must point to an array with capacity for at least MAX_HEADERS (10) entries; more than 10 headers will cause the function to return 0 (parse failure).
On successful parse, headers are written sequentially; after the last header, the function sets the next headers->first to an empty string_view (nullptr, length 0) to mark termination.
Returned value is the number of bytes consumed from postPaddedBuffer to just after the terminating CRLF; callers should advance their cursor by this many bytes.
The string_views in headers alias the original buffer; the buffer must outlive any use of those views.
On error, the function returns 0; callers must treat 0 as failure and not consume any bytes.

functions.name: uWS::ParameterParser::ParameterParser
functions.description: Constructs a stateful parameter parser over a header-like line (commonly a Content-Disposition header) and prepares it to iterate key/value parameters separated by ';' and '='. Values may be quoted and are unquoted during parsing. The parser does not copy the data; it stores a std::string_view into the provided line and consumes it as getKeyValue is called.
requirements: The memory referenced by 'line' must remain valid and unchanged for the lifetime of the ParameterParser and for all subsequent calls to getKeyValue.
The input should contain parameters separated by ';' with key=value tokens; quoted-string values are supported, but malformed quoting may end parsing early.
Do not use the same ParameterParser instance concurrently from multiple threads (the parser is stateful).

functions.name: uWS::ParameterParser::getKeyValue
functions.description: Returns the next key/value pair parsed from the remaining line. Values may be empty, and quoted values are returned without surrounding quotes. When the returned key (first) is empty, parsing has reached the end. Repeatedly call until the key is empty to iterate all parameters.
requirements: Must be called on a valid ParameterParser that was constructed with a still-valid backing buffer (the original line's data must outlive these calls).
This function is stateful and consumes internal input; do not expect idempotent results across calls.
Not thread-safe; avoid concurrent calls on the same instance.

functions.name: uWS::MultipartParser::MultipartParser
functions.description: Constructs a multipart/form-data parser by extracting the boundary from a Content-Type header value. It validates that the type starts with "multipart/" and that a boundary string (length 1..70) follows an '='. The boundary is copied into an internal buffer prefixed with "--" for later matching.
requirements: 'contentType' should be a full Content-Type header value beginning with "multipart/" and containing a boundary parameter using '=' (e.g., "multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary...").
Boundary length must be between 1 and 70 characters; otherwise the parser will be invalid (isValid() returns false).
Call isValid() after construction to verify that a boundary was successfully parsed.

functions.name: uWS::MultipartParser::isValid
functions.description: Returns true if a boundary was successfully parsed during construction, indicating the parser is ready to parse a multipart body.
requirements: Must be called on an initialized MultipartParser instance.
If false, do not call setBody/getNextPart; fix the Content-Type or boundary first.

functions.name: uWS::MultipartParser::setBody
functions.description: Sets the complete raw multipart message body to be parsed in subsequent getNextPart calls. The body must include the boundary delimiters and CRLF framing as received on the wire.
requirements: Must be called before the first call to getNextPart.
The memory referenced by 'body' must remain valid and unchanged for the entire parsing sequence (until parsing is finished).
The 'body' buffer must be writable (non-const memory): getNextPart will write a '\r' byte just after each extracted part segment to aid header parsing.
Provide the full multipart payload, including the initial boundary line, part headers and bodies, CRLFs, and closing boundary markers.

functions.name: uWS::MultipartParser::getNextPart
functions.description: Parses and returns the next part's body as a string_view and fills the provided headers array with parsed header key/value pairs for that part. Returns std::nullopt when no more parts are available or on parse error. The function consumes internal state; iteration is strictly single-pass. Header parsing consumes bytes from the part up to the blank line ("\r\n\r\n").
requirements: isValid() must return true prior to calling; otherwise behavior is an immediate end or parse failure.
setBody() must have been called with the full multipart payload before the first call.

'headers' must be a non-null pointer to a writable array of std::pair<std::string_view,std::string_view> with sufficient capacity to hold all headers for a part plus any terminator expected by the underlying header parser (exact required capacity is not documented here).
The underlying 'body' memory must be writable: this function writes a '\r' byte immediately after the part slice to assist parsing.
The multipart body must contain proper CRLF framing around boundaries and between headers and body ("\r\n\r\n").
Do not attempt to iterate parts more than once or rewind; the parser mutates internal state and the input buffer for a single forward pass.
Treat std::nullopt as either end-of-input or parse error; callers should differentiate using external context if needed.

functions.name: uWS::getDecodedQueryValue
functions.signature: static inline std::string_view uWS::getDecodedQueryValue(std::string_view key, std::string_view rawQuery)
functions.description: Parses a URI query string (expected to include the leading '?'), searches for the exact key, and returns the percent-decoded value as a std::string_view that points into, and may modify, the provided buffer. Values are decoded in place: %XX sequences are converted to a single byte and '+' becomes a space. Keys are compared byte-for-byte (no decoding, case-sensitive). The returned view aliases the input storage and is only valid as long as that storage remains alive and unmodified. If the key is found with an empty value, an empty view with a non-null data() is returned; if the key is not found or certain parse errors occur, a view with data()==nullptr and size()==0 is returned. On malformed percent-encodings (e.g., '%' not followed by two hex digits), an empty default-constructed view is returned.
requirements: key must be non-empty; otherwise the function returns an empty default-constructed std::string_view
rawQuery should include the leading '?' character; the parser starts scanning from index 1 and treats '&' as a separator
rawQuery must refer to writable, contiguous memory; the function decodes in place and may write NUL and other bytes into the underlying buffer
The underlying memory of rawQuery must remain valid and unmodified for the lifetime of the returned std::string_view; the view aliases the input buffer

Query items are expected in the form key=value separated by '&'; if a candidate item (same first character as key) lacks '=', the function returns a {nullptr,0} view indicating an invalid query string
Keys are matched exactly (case-sensitive, no percent-decoding)
Percent-encoded values must have '%' followed by two hexadecimal digits; otherwise the function returns a default-constructed empty std::string_view

A returned empty value is represented by a view of size 0 with a non-null data() pointer (i.e., present but empty). Not found and some error cases are indicated by data()==nullptr and size()==0; callers should check data()!=nullptr to distinguish an empty-but-present value from not found/error

functions.name: uWS::chunkSize
functions.description: Extracts the current chunk size (in bytes) encoded in the parser state by masking off state flags. Intended to be used with the other helpers operating on the same state word.
requirements: Argument state may be any 64-bit value; no preconditions.
The returned value is the raw masked size field and may be zero.

functions.name: uWS::consumeHexNumber
functions.description: Parses a hexadecimal chunk-size line from the start of data, updates state with the parsed size and flags, and advances data past the terminating LF. If invalid hex digits or size overflow are encountered, sets state to an error sentinel. Note: despite the comment suggesting a return of bytes consumed, this function returns void and communicates via its out-parameters.
requirements: data must reference a buffer whose contents remain valid during the call.
data is modified in-place via remove_prefix to skip the parsed header line and any characters up to and including the first '\n'.
state is updated in place; on invalid input it is set to STATE_IS_ERROR (~0ull).
Input is expected to start at a chunk-size line (hex digits optionally followed by extensions), terminated by CRLF; non-compliant input may set error state.
Behavior relies on ASCII semantics for hex parsing.

functions.name: uWS::decChunkSize
functions.signature: inline void uWS::decChunkSize(uint64_t &state, unsigned int by)
functions.description: Decrements the size field embedded in state by the specified amount, preserving non-size flags. Used to track remaining bytes in the current chunk.
requirements: by should not exceed the current chunk size (chunkSize(state)) to avoid underflowing the size field.
state should currently contain a valid size field; calling with an invalid/error state will produce meaningless results.

functions.name: uWS::hasChunkSize
functions.description: Returns true if the parser state indicates a chunk size has been fully parsed and is available.
requirements: state may be any value; no preconditions.

functions.name: uWS::isParsingChunkedEncoding
functions.description: Returns true if the state indicates the parser is in the middle of parsing chunked encoding (i.e., any relevant flags are set).
requirements: state may be any value; no preconditions.

functions.name: uWS::isParsingInvalidChunkedEncoding
functions.description: Returns true if the state equals the error sentinel, meaning an invalid chunked encoding was detected during parsing.
requirements: state may be any value; no preconditions.

functions.name: uWS::getNextChunk
functions.signature: static std::optional<std::string_view> uWS::getNextChunk(std::string_view &data, uint64_t &state, bool trailer = false)
functions.description: Consumes from data and advances the parser state to produce the next available chunk payload segment according to HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer encoding. Returns a string_view to the next chunk payload (which may be empty for the terminating 0-sized chunk) or std::nullopt when no emit-ready data is available or when parsing must stop (including on error). It also handles CRLF delimiters and optionally trailer consumption when trailer is true.
requirements: data must reference a contiguous buffer containing chunked-encoding bytes; the underlying storage must outlive any returned string_view.
data is modified in-place (remove_prefix) to reflect consumed bytes; callers must preserve state across calls to continue parsing the same message.
Initialize state to 0 before parsing a new message; pass the same state by reference across successive calls.
On invalid input, state is set to STATE_IS_ERROR and std::nullopt is returned; callers should check isParsingInvalidChunkedEncoding(state) after a nullopt to detect error.
Returned std::string_view aliases the original buffer; do not free or mutate the underlying memory while using the view.

Do not assume std::nullopt always signals end-of-message; it can also mean more input is needed. Continue feeding data and calling until the terminating empty chunk has been observed and subsequent calls drop into trailer handling (if enabled) or state resets.

If trailer is true, the function will enter a mode that drops trailer bytes after the terminating chunk until CRLF is fully consumed; callers relying on trailer parsing must keep calling until std::nullopt with state reset to 0 indicates completion.

functions.name: uWS::ChunkIterator::ChunkIterator
functions.description: Constructs a chunk iterator over a chunked-encoded buffer and parsing state. Immediately fetches the first available chunk by invoking uWS::getNextChunk on the provided data/state.
requirements: data must be a non-null pointer to a valid std::string_view whose underlying storage outlives the iterator and any yielded string_view.
state must be a non-null pointer to a valid uint64_t state word, initialized appropriately (typically 0 for a new message) and preserved for the iterator’s lifetime.
If trailer parsing is desired, pass trailer = true; otherwise leave default false.
The pointed-to data and state will be mutated during iteration.

functions.name: uWS::ChunkIterator::begin
functions.description: Returns a copy of this iterator as the begin iterator for range-style iteration.
requirements: Call on a properly constructed iterator (non-default) if you intend to iterate.
The returned iterator shares the same underlying data/state pointers and will advance them as it iterates.

functions.name: uWS::ChunkIterator::end
functions.description: Returns a default-constructed sentinel iterator representing the end of the sequence.
requirements: None beyond typical iterator usage; compare against this sentinel to detect end of iteration.

functions.name: uWS::ChunkIterator::operator*
functions.description: Dereferences the iterator to access the current chunk payload view.
requirements: Must only be called when the iterator is valid (i.e., not equal to end()).
If called when there is no current chunk (chunk.has_value() == false), the function aborts the process (std::abort).
The returned string_view references the underlying buffer; ensure it remains valid while in use.

functions.name: uWS::ChunkIterator::operator!=
functions.description: Compares two iterators for inequality based on whether they have a current chunk value. Primarily used to compare against the end sentinel.
requirements: At least one of the iterators should be a valid iterator from the same iteration context; comparing with a default-constructed end sentinel is supported.
No additional preconditions.

functions.name: uWS::ChunkIterator::operator++
functions.description: Advances the iterator to the next available chunk by invoking uWS::getNextChunk on the underlying data/state.
requirements: Must not be called on an end/sentinel iterator (where chunk.has_value() == false); doing so will dereference null pointers internally and likely crash.
The underlying data and state pointers must remain valid for the duration of iteration.

data_types.description: A writable buffer containing one or more RFC 822/HTTP-style header lines, each formatted as `Key: Value` terminated by CRLF, and ending with an empty line (CRLF). Keys consist of token characters; values are visible ASCII excluding CR/LF. The entire section is contiguous and mutable.

A single header-like parameter string consisting of semicolon- and equals-separated tokens, e.g., `form-data; name="field"; filename="foo.txt"`. Supports optional quoting with double quotes and optional whitespace around separators.

A raw HTTP multipart body containing boundary-delimited parts, including boundary lines that start with `--<boundary>`, CRLF framing, per-part headers followed by a blank line (CRLF CRLF), and part payloads. The buffer must be writable because parsers may modify or pad bytes.
Unstructured byte buffer with no required format. May contain any bytes and is used in contexts where the function can accept or ignore arbitrary content.

A Content-Type header string value, e.g., `multipart/form-data; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary...` or other media types. For multipart parsing, it must start with `multipart/` and include a `boundary=` parameter of length 1..70.

A URI query component beginning with `?` followed by key-value pairs separated by `&` in the form `key=value`, where values may contain percent-encodings (%XX) and '+' as space. The buffer must be writable for in-place decoding.
A single line encoding an HTTP chunk size in hexadecimal, optionally followed by chunk extensions after a semicolon, and terminated by CRLF. Example: `1A;ext=val\r\n`.

A full HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer-encoded payload: one or more chunks of the form `<hex-size>
<payload>
`, followed by a terminating `0
` and a final `
` after optional trailers. Used as a contiguous buffer for incremental parsing.

generators.generator:
import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for an HTTP header section suitable for uWS::getHeaders
# Constraints:
# - Writable contiguous bytes
# - 0..10 headers, each: Key ": " Value "\r\n"
# - Final terminating "\r\n"
# - Keys are tokens (A-Za-z0-9-), non-empty
# - Values are visible ASCII excluding CR/LF (HT allowed); may be empty
# - Keep total size <= 4096 bytes

# Character sets
_KEY_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-"
# Visible ASCII 0x20..0x7E excluding CR/LF; allow TAB (0x09) as well
_VALUE_CHARS = "\t" + "".join(chr(c) for c in range(32, 127) if c not in (10, 13))

# Some interesting canonical header names/values to trigger different paths
_INTERESTING_HEADERS: List[Tuple[str, str]] = [
    ("Host", "example.com"),
    ("Content-Type", "text/plain; charset=UTF-8"),
    ("Content-Length", "0"),
    ("X-Custom-Header", "value"),
    ("Accept", "*/*"),
    ("User-Agent", "uWS-Fuzzer/1.0"),
    ("Transfer-Encoding", "chunked"),
    ("Connection", "keep-alive"),
    ("Content-Disposition", "form-data; name=\"field\"; filename=\"a.txt\""),
]

def _rand_key(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 32) -> str:
    # Ensure non-empty and token-compliant
    n = rng.randint(1, max_len)
    return "".join(rng.choice(_KEY_CHARS) for _ in range(n))

def _rand_value(rng: random.Random, max_len: int = 96) -> str:
    # Values may be empty
    # Bias to include separators, quotes and parameters which downstream might parse
    specials = ["; charset=UTF-8", "; q=0.5", "; boundary=----WebKitFormBoundary7MA4YWxkTrZu0gW", ", gzip", ", deflate", "" ]
    # 40% choose from specials appended to base
    base_len = rng.randint(0, max_len)
    base = "".join(rng.choice(_VALUE_CHARS) for _ in range(base_len))
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        base += rng.choice(specials)
    # Strip any CR/LF just in case (should not be present from set)
    return base.replace("\r", " ").replace("\n", " ")

def _emit_header_line(key: str, value: str) -> bytes:
    return (key + ": " + value + "\r\n").encode("ascii", errors="ignore")

def _build_headers(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Decide number of headers 0..10, with some bias towards non-zero
    n = rng.choices(range(0, 11), weights=[1] + [3]*10, k=1)[0]

    buf = bytearray()

    # Optionally inject some interesting predefined headers
    presets = _INTERESTING_HEADERS.copy()
    rng.shuffle(presets)
    preset_count = min(len(presets), n, rng.randint(0, min(5, n)))
    for i in range(preset_count):
        k, v = presets[i]
        line = _emit_header_line(k, v)
        if len(buf) + len(line) + 2 > 4096:
            break
        buf += line

    # Fill the rest with randomized but valid headers
    remaining = max(0, n - preset_count)
    for _ in range(remaining):
        k = _rand_key(rng)
        v = _rand_value(rng)
        line = _emit_header_line(k, v)
        if len(buf) + len(line) + 2 > 4096:
            break
        buf += line

    # Always add terminating empty line CRLF
    if len(buf) + 2 > 4096:
        # If somehow at limit, trim last header line conservatively to make room
        # Remove bytes until we can add CRLF; if buffer too small, just reset to empty
        while len(buf) + 2 > 4096 and len(buf) > 0:
            # remove last byte until previous CRLF or empty
            buf = buf[:-1]
        # Ensure it ends at a header boundary; if last line corrupted, drop all
        if not buf.endswith(b"\r\n"):
            buf = bytearray()
    buf += b"\r\n"

    return bytes(buf)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Occasionally craft special scenarios to exercise parser behavior:
    mode = rng.random()

    if mode < 0.15:
        # Minimal: only terminator (no headers)
        return b"\r\n"
    elif mode < 0.35:
        # Single header with empty value
        key = _rand_key(rng, 16)
        line = _emit_header_line(key, "") + b"\r\n"
        return line
    elif mode < 0.55:
        # Max headers (10) with short values
        rng2 = random.Random(rng.randint(0, 2**32 - 1))
        buf = bytearray()
        for _ in range(10):
            k = _rand_key(rng2, 16)
            v = _rand_value(rng2, 12)
            line = _emit_header_line(k, v)
            if len(buf) + len(line) + 2 > 4096:
                break
            buf += line
        buf += b"\r\n"
        return bytes(buf)
    elif mode < 0.75:
        # Include headers that commonly appear in multipart to pair with MultipartParser later
        buf = bytearray()
        ct_value = "multipart/form-data; boundary=---------------------------" + str(seed % 100000).zfill(5)
        lines = [
            _emit_header_line("Content-Type", ct_value),
            _emit_header_line("Content-Disposition", "form-data; name=\"file\"; filename=\"f.txt\""),
            _emit_header_line("Content-Length", str((seed % 997) + 1)),
        ]
        for line in lines:
            if len(buf) + len(line) + 2 > 4096:
                break
            buf += line
        buf += b"\r\n"
        return bytes(buf)
    else:
        # General randomized header block
        return _build_headers(rng)

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# We want to generate interesting but valid multipart bodies that the stub can use when it knows the boundary
# The stub constructs a body itself when it already knows the boundary; however FUZZ_PARAM_STR is used for data
# within the part body, or as the whole body when no boundary/isValid are set. Our generator returns a bytes blob
# that is useful in both cases:
# - Often: a standalone multipart body with common boundary patterns and CRLF framing
# - Sometimes: short ASCII or binary payloads for the fallback path
# The stub may cap sizes (64 for data, 512 for arbitrary). Keep overall size <= 4096.

CRLF = b"\r\n"

ASCII_PRINTABLE = bytes([c for c in range(32, 127)])
BINARY_BYTES = bytes(range(256))


def _rand_boundary(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    # Common boundary styles (similar to browsers) with allowed length 1..70
    choices = [
        "----WebKitFormBoundary" + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(8, 24))),
        "---------------------------" + ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(12, 24))),
        ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_'()+,-./:=?") for _ in range(rng.randint(6, 32))).strip(),
        "boundary" + ''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 10)))
    ]
    # Ensure 1..70
    b = rng.choice(choices)
    if len(b) == 0:
        b = "b"
    if len(b) > 70:
        b = b[:70]
    return b


def _header_lines(rng: random.Random) -> List[Tuple[str, str]]:
    # Some typical multipart headers
    headers: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    # Always include a Content-Disposition with parameters to exercise ParameterParser elsewhere
    name = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 10)))
    disp = "form-data"
    # Sometimes quoted filename
    parts = [f"name=\"{name}\""]
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        fname = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "._-") for _ in range(rng.randint(3, 12)))
        parts.append(f"filename=\"{fname}\"")
    headers.append(("Content-Disposition", f"{disp}; " + "; ".join(parts)))

    # Optionally a content-type
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        ct = rng.choice(["text/plain", "application/octet-stream", "application/json", "image/png"])
        headers.append(("Content-Type", ct))

    # Add one arbitrary header to trigger getHeaders parsing with multiple lines
    if rng.random() < 0.8:
        headers.append(("X-Custom", ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_/:.") for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 20)))))

    return headers


def _encode_headers(headers: List[Tuple[str, str]]) -> bytes:
    out = bytearray()
    for k, v in headers:
        out.extend(k.encode('ascii', 'ignore'))
        out.extend(b": ")
        out.extend(v.encode('ascii', 'ignore'))
        out.extend(CRLF)
    out.extend(CRLF)  # end of headers
    return bytes(out)


def _random_part_body(rng: random.Random, target_len: int) -> bytes:
    # Build an interesting small payload (<= target_len)
    modes = ["ascii", "binary", "json", "repeated", "hex"]
    mode = rng.choice(modes)
    if mode == "ascii":
        s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.printable[:-6]) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, target_len)))
        return s.encode()
    if mode == "binary":
        # Slice of 0..255 pattern
        rep = rng.randint(1, max(1, target_len // 256 + 1))
        data = (BINARY_BYTES * rep)[:target_len]
        return data
    if mode == "json":
        # Small JSON text
        keys = ["a", "msg", "id", "ok", "n"]
        obj = {rng.choice(keys): rng.choice([True, False, rng.randint(0, 9999), ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(rng.randint(0, 12)))]) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 4))}
        s = str(obj).replace("'", '"')
        return s[:target_len].encode()
    if mode == "repeated":
        token = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 8))).encode()
        return (token * (target_len // max(1, len(token)) + 1))[:target_len]
    if mode == "hex":
        # hex string to pair with u32/u64 conversion testing contexts
        val = rng.getrandbits(rng.randint(4, 64))
        s = format(val, 'x')
        return s[:target_len].encode()
    return b""


def _build_multipart(rng: random.Random, parts: int) -> bytes:
    boundary = _rand_boundary(rng)
    boundary_line = ("--" + boundary).encode()
    buf = bytearray()

    # Initial boundary line
    buf.extend(boundary_line)
    buf.extend(CRLF)

    for i in range(parts):
        hdrs = _header_lines(rng)
        buf.extend(_encode_headers(hdrs))
        body_len = rng.randint(0, 64)
        body = _random_part_body(rng, body_len)
        buf.extend(body)
        buf.extend(CRLF)
        # Next boundary (non-closing) after each part to match stub expectations
        buf.extend(boundary_line)
        buf.extend(CRLF)

    # Keep under size; this structure already has the trailing boundary line as the stub expects
    return bytes(buf)


def _build_fallback_payload(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Arbitrary but interesting data <= 512 bytes; include CRLFs to look header-like sometimes
    length = rng.randint(0, 512)
    chunks: List[bytes] = []
    while sum(len(c) for c in chunks) < length:
        kind = rng.choice(["ascii", "crlf", "binary", "digits", "url"])
        remain = length - sum(len(c) for c in chunks)
        if remain <= 0:
            break
        take = rng.randint(1, min(64, remain))
        if kind == "ascii":
            s = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " -_:./") for _ in range(take))
            chunks.append(s.encode())
        elif kind == "crlf":
            line = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(max(0, take - 2)))
            chunks.append(line.encode() + CRLF)
        elif kind == "binary":
            chunks.append(bytes(rng.getrandbits(8) for _ in range(take)))
        elif kind == "digits":
            chunks.append(''.join(rng.choice(string.digits) for _ in range(take)).encode())
        else:  # url
            base = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(max(1, take // 2)))
            q = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "&=%+") for _ in range(take - len(base)))
            chunks.append((base + "?" + q)[:take].encode())
    return b"".join(chunks)[:512]


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)

    # Choose a strategy: multipart vs arbitrary buffer
    strategy = rng.choices(["multipart", "fallback"], weights=[0.7, 0.3], k=1)[0]

    if strategy == "multipart":
        parts = rng.randint(1, 3)  # small number of parts to stay tiny
        data = _build_multipart(rng, parts)
        # Safety cap
        return data[:4096]
    else:
        return _build_fallback_payload(rng)[:4096]

import random
import string
from typing import List

# Target data type: HTTP Content-Type header value for multipart parsing.
# The fuzzer stub constructs a MultipartParser from a provided Content-Type string.
# It explores three modes: valid, invalid prefix, invalid boundary size.
# Our generator should provide interesting, valid Content-Type header values that
# often exercise the valid path, but can also occasionally hit edge cases like
# 1-char boundary, 70-char boundary, unusual token characters, and common real-world
# boundaries. The stub itself may also mutate to invalid modes, but our input should
# be valid and well-formed on its own.

# We generate a single bytes buffer intended to be used by FUZZ_PARAM_STR.
# Design:
# - With weighted probability, emit:
#   - Typical browser-style long boundary (WebKit-style)
#   - Minimal boundary length 1
#   - Max boundary length 70
#   - Random boundary of mixed token-safe chars used by stub
#   - Alternative multipart subtype (e.g., multipart/mixed) still valid
#   - Include extra parameters before/after boundary to exercise parser's naive '=' search
# - Avoid CR/LF or quotes in boundary; only token chars.
# - Overall length under 4096 bytes.

TOKEN_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.+/ ?"  # matches stub allowance (space optional but safe in params around '=')
# However boundary itself should avoid spaces per stub building; we will not include space in boundary token itself.
BOUNDARY_CHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "-_.+/?"

REALISTIC_PREFIXES = [
    "multipart/form-data",
    "multipart/mixed",
    "multipart/related",
    "multipart/alternative",
    "multipart/report",
]

WEBKIT_PREFIX = "----WebKitFormBoundary"


def _rand_boundary(rng: random.Random, length: int) -> str:
    return ''.join(rng.choice(BOUNDARY_CHARS) for _ in range(length))


def _webkit_boundary(rng: random.Random, min_tail: int = 12, max_tail: int = 24) -> str:
    tail_len = rng.randint(min_tail, max_tail)
    tail = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(tail_len))
    return WEBKIT_PREFIX + tail


def _build_params(rng: random.Random, boundary: str) -> str:
    # Compose parameters with optional extras placed before/after boundary
    params: List[str] = []
    # Optional charset parameter
    if rng.random() < 0.4:
        params.append('charset=' + rng.choice(['utf-8', 'iso-8859-1', 'us-ascii']))
    # Optional name/filename parameters (typical in Content-Disposition, but harmless here)
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        params.append('format=' + rng.choice(['flowed', 'fixed']))
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        params.append('type=' + rng.choice(['text/plain', 'application/json']))
    # Insert boundary parameter; avoid quotes, keep simple per parser assumptions
    # Parser looks for '=' after index 10, so ensure boundary= appears plainly.
    # We may place other params before to test '=' scanning still finds the last/first '='.
    # But since the implementation takes substring from the first '=' after 10 to end,
    # we place boundary= last most of the time to ensure it is picked up correctly.
    if rng.random() < 0.7:
        # Place extras before boundary
        pass
    else:
        # Place some extras after boundary (still fine as parser takes from first '=')
        pass
    params.append('boundary=' + boundary)
    # Maybe add a trailing harmless parameter after boundary; parser ignores but still okay
    if rng.random() < 0.2:
        params.append('delsp=' + rng.choice(['yes', 'no']))
    return '; '.join(params)


def _build_content_type(rng: random.Random) -> str:
    p = rng.random()
    prefix = rng.choice(REALISTIC_PREFIXES)

    # Choose boundary scenario
    if p < 0.20:
        # Minimal length 1
        boundary = _rand_boundary(rng, 1)
    elif p < 0.40:
        # Max length 70
        boundary = _rand_boundary(rng, 70)
    elif p < 0.65:
        # WebKit-like
        # Ensure total length <= 70 per parser; WEBKIT_PREFIX is 22 chars, tail chosen accordingly
        max_tail = max(1, 70 - len(WEBKIT_PREFIX))
        min_tail = min(24, max_tail)
        # pick tail within [min_tail, max_tail]
        tail_len = rng.randint(min_tail, max_tail)
        boundary = WEBKIT_PREFIX + ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters + string.digits) for _ in range(tail_len))
    else:
        # Random medium length
        boundary = _rand_boundary(rng, rng.randint(5, 40))

    params = _build_params(rng, boundary)
    return f"{prefix}; {params}"


def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    # With small probability, generate an alternative valid header format variants
    # like extra whitespace or uppercase/lowercase mixing (prefix must still start with 'multipart/')
    header = _build_content_type(rng)

    # Randomly vary casing of 'multipart' sub-type prefix after the slash is okay; must keep 'multipart/' exact
    # The constructor checks contentType.substr(0,10) == "multipart/"
    # So we must NOT alter the first 10 characters.
    # We can vary case in subtype name (after 10th char) and parameters.
    if rng.random() < 0.3:
        # randomize subtype casing beyond the fixed 'multipart/'
        fixed = 'multipart/'
        rest = header[len(fixed):]
        rest = ''.join(ch.upper() if rng.random() < 0.3 else ch.lower() if ch.isalpha() else ch for ch in rest)
        header = fixed + rest

    # Ensure total size <= 4096
    if len(header) > 4000:
        header = header[:4000]

    return header.encode('ascii', errors='ignore')

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for URL query strings suitable for uWS::getDecodedQueryValue fuzz stub
# - Must begin with '?'
# - Contain key=value pairs separated by '&'
# - Values may include percent-encodings (%XX) and '+' which decodes to space
# - Buffer should be valid UTF-8 bytes but only requirement is writable bytes; we'll return bytes
# - Keep size <= 4096

_HEX = '0123456789ABCDEF'
_SAFE_KCHARS = string.ascii_letters + string.digits + "_-.~"
_SAFE_VCHARS = _SAFE_KCHARS + ":/@$!*'(),"  # allow some extra safe-ish characters

def _rand_percent_encoded(r: random.Random) -> str:
    # Return %XX with random byte encoded uppercase hex (common)
    b = r.randrange(0, 256)
    return '%' + _HEX[(b >> 4) & 0xF] + _HEX[b & 0xF]

def _rand_key(r: random.Random, min_len=1, max_len=16) -> str:
    # Keys should not include '&' or '=' per stub sanitization
    # Mix of safe chars; occasionally include percent-encoded in key to ensure non-decoding of key path
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts = []
    for _ in range(length):
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.85:
            parts.append(r.choice(_SAFE_KCHARS))
        elif choice < 0.90:
            # Include doted segments
            parts.append('.')
        else:
            # Rare percent in key (note: keys are not decoded by target; but '%' should be fine)
            parts.append('%')
    # Ensure non-empty and not starting with separators
    k = ''.join(parts)
    if not k:
        k = 'k'
    # Avoid stray '=' and '&' entirely
    k = k.replace('=', 'x').replace('&', 'x')
    return k

def _rand_value(r: random.Random, min_len=0, max_len=64) -> str:
    length = r.randint(min_len, max_len)
    parts: List[str] = []
    i = 0
    while i < length:
        choice = r.random()
        if choice < 0.60:
            parts.append(r.choice(_SAFE_VCHARS))
            i += 1
        elif choice < 0.75:
            parts.append('+')  # decodes to space
            i += 1
        else:
            enc = _rand_percent_encoded(r)
            parts.append(enc)
            i += len(enc)
    return ''.join(parts)

def _make_pair(r: random.Random) -> Tuple[str, str]:
    # Sometimes produce empty value or empty key scenarios
    mode = r.randrange(0, 8)
    if mode == 0:
        # empty value
        k = _rand_key(r)
        v = ''
    elif mode == 1:
        # short key/value
        k = _rand_key(r, 1, 6)
        v = _rand_value(r, 0, 12)
    elif mode == 2:
        # value-heavy with many encodings
        k = _rand_key(r, 1, 10)
        v = ''.join(_rand_percent_encoded(r) if r.random() < 0.6 else r.choice(_SAFE_VCHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(5, 20)))
    elif mode == 3:
        # plus-heavy
        k = _rand_key(r)
        v = '++'.join(_rand_value(r, 0, 5) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 5)))
    elif mode == 4:
        # numeric value
        k = _rand_key(r)
        v = str(r.randrange(0, 1 << 32))
    elif mode == 5:
        # unicode-like percent encodings for common UTF-8 bytes
        k = _rand_key(r)
        raw = 'こんにちは世界'  # will percent-encode bytes
        v = ''.join('%%%02X' % b for b in raw.encode('utf-8'))
    elif mode == 6:
        # path-ish value
        k = _rand_key(r)
        segs = [ ''.join(r.choice(_SAFE_VCHARS) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 6))) for _ in range(r.randint(1, 4)) ]
        v = '/'.join(segs)
    else:
        k = _rand_key(r)
        v = _rand_value(r)
    return k, v

def _build_query(r: random.Random, target_key: str) -> str:
    # Construct a query beginning with '?', ensuring at least one pair, and include a pair for target_key
    pairs: List[Tuple[str, str]] = []
    # Chance to include multiple occurrences of target_key; parser returns first exact match
    occurrences = 1 + (1 if r.random() < 0.3 else 0)
    for _ in range(occurrences):
        # Ensure target key uses exact key string
        val = _rand_value(r, 0, 32)
        pairs.append((target_key, val))
    # Add random other pairs
    extra = r.randint(0, 6)
    for _ in range(extra):
        k, v = _make_pair(r)
        # Avoid accidental duplicate keys overshadowing variety; allow sometimes
        pairs.append((k, v))
    # Randomize order
    r.shuffle(pairs)
    # Assemble
    buf_parts: List[str] = ['?']
    for i, (k, v) in enumerate(pairs):
        if i:
            buf_parts.append('&')
        buf_parts.append(k)
        buf_parts.append('=')
        buf_parts.append(v)
    return ''.join(buf_parts)

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    r = random.Random(seed)

    # Decide on strategy relative to fuzzer stub behavior
    # The stub may clear key to empty depending on its own FUZZ_PARAM; we provide a buffer that remains valid
    # We'll sometimes produce queries crafted to exercise decoding and boundary cases.

    # Choose a key likely to be accepted by stub (no '&' or '=') and non-empty
    key = _rand_key(r, 1, 16)

    # Construct a plausible query
    query = _build_query(r, key)

    # Size guard: if too large, trim by removing pairs from the end while keeping at least the first
    if len(query) > 4000:
        # naive trim: keep prefix until below limit, ensure it ends not in middle of percent-encoding
        query = query[:4000]
        # Avoid trailing lone '%' which could be malformed; drop it
        if query.endswith('%'):
            query = query[:-1]
        # Also avoid ending with '%' followed by one hex
        if len(query) >= 2 and query[-2] == '%':
            query = query[:-2]

    # Ensure query has at least one pair after '?'
    if len(query) <= 1:
        query = '?a='

    # Return bytes; buffer is ASCII-compatible
    return query.encode('utf-8')

import random
import string
from typing import List, Tuple

# Generator for valid HTTP/1.1 chunked transfer-encoded payloads.
# This targets uWS::getNextChunk and uWS::ChunkIterator fuzzers which
# build a chunked message as: "<hex>\r\n<payload>\r\n0\r\n\r\n".
# We generate similar but richer valid messages to exercise code paths:
# - various chunk sizes (including 0-sized mid-stream chunk is not allowed by RFC, so avoid until final)
# - multiple chunks
# - optional chunk extensions (allowed by spec; parsers should skip)
# - optional trailers before the final CRLF
# - payload character variety
# - optional inclusion of LF-only within payload (legal as data)
# - keep total size <= 4096

_HEX = '0123456789abcdef'

def _rand_ascii_bytes(rng: random.Random, n: int) -> bytes:
    # Mix of visible ASCII plus some spaces and punctuation, excluding CR to avoid accidental framing
    alphabet = (
        string.ascii_letters + string.digits + " \t" + "_-.:/?&=+*@#,$!()[]{}|" + "\n\t"
    )
    return ''.join(rng.choice(alphabet) for _ in range(n)).encode('utf-8')

def _make_chunk(rng: random.Random, size: int, with_ext: bool) -> bytes:
    # Build a single chunk with optional extensions
    assert size >= 0
    payload = _rand_ascii_bytes(rng, size)
    ext = b''
    if with_ext and rng.random() < 0.7:
        # RFC allows ";name=value" extensions; keep ASCII tokens
        parts: List[bytes] = []
        for _ in range(rng.randint(1, 3)):
            klen = rng.randint(1, 6)
            vlen = rng.randint(0, 8)
            key = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits) for _ in range(klen)).encode()
            if rng.random() < 0.6:
                if rng.random() < 0.5:
                    val = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits) for _ in range(vlen)).encode()
                else:
                    # quoted-string value; ensure no quotes inside
                    qv = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits+" -_./") for _ in range(vlen)).encode()
                    val = b'"' + qv + b'"'
                parts.append(b';' + key + b'=' + val)
            else:
                parts.append(b';' + key)
        ext = b''.join(parts)
    size_hex = format(size, 'x').encode('ascii')
    return size_hex + ext + b"\r\n" + payload + b"\r\n"

def _make_trailers(rng: random.Random) -> bytes:
    # Generate 0-3 simple RFC 822 style header lines as trailers
    n = rng.randint(0, 3)
    if n == 0:
        return b"\r\n"
    lines: List[bytes] = []
    for _ in range(n):
        klen = rng.randint(2, 8)
        vlen = rng.randint(0, 16)
        key = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_letters) for _ in range(klen)).lower().encode('ascii')
        # Values may be empty
        if vlen == 0:
            val = b''
        else:
            val = _rand_ascii_bytes(rng, vlen)
            # Avoid CR and ensure no stray CRLF sequences other than the terminator
            val = val.replace(b'\r', b' ').replace(b'\n', b' ')
        lines.append(key + b': ' + val + b"\r\n")
    return b''.join(lines) + b"\r\n"

def _plan_chunks(rng: random.Random, budget: int) -> List[Tuple[int, bool]]:
    # Return list of (size, with_ext) for chunks such that total fits within budget
    # Keep sizes modest to improve chances of multiple chunks
    chunks: List[Tuple[int, bool]] = []
    # Reserve space for final \r\n0\r\n and potential trailers; approximate 64 bytes
    remain = max(0, budget - 64)
    # Choose 1..5 chunks
    cnt = rng.randint(1, 5)
    for i in range(cnt):
        if remain <= 0:
            break
        # Choose size 0..128 but non-zero for all non-final chunks
        max_size = min(128, remain // 2 + 1)
        if max_size <= 0:
            break
        size = rng.randint(1, max(1, max_size))
        with_ext = rng.random() < 0.8
        # Estimate overhead: hex (up to 3 bytes typical), CRLF x2 and extensions (~10)
        est = len(format(size, 'x')) + 2 + size + 2 + (10 if with_ext else 0)
        if est > remain and size > 1:
            size = max(1, remain - 16)
            est = len(format(size, 'x')) + 14 + size
        if est > remain:
            break
        chunks.append((size, with_ext))
        remain -= est
    if not chunks:
        # Ensure at least one tiny chunk
        chunks.append((1, False))
    return chunks

def generate(seed: int) -> bytes:
    rng = random.Random(seed)
    budget = 4096

    chunks_plan = _plan_chunks(rng, budget)
    parts: List[bytes] = []
    for size, with_ext in chunks_plan:
        parts.append(_make_chunk(rng, size, with_ext))

    # Final zero-size chunk with optional extensions (valid: extensions allowed on last chunk)
    last_ext = b''
    if rng.random() < 0.6:
        # include an extension on the terminating chunk
        k = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(1,5))).encode()
        v = ''.join(rng.choice(string.ascii_lowercase+string.digits) for _ in range(rng.randint(0,6))).encode()
        if rng.random() < 0.5:
            last_ext = b';' + k + (b'=' + v if len(v)>0 else b'')
        else:
            last_ext = b';' + k + b'="' + v + b'"'

    message = b''.join(parts) + b"0" + last_ext + b"\r\n"

    # Optional trailers then final CRLF
    trailers = _make_trailers(rng)
    message += trailers

    # Safety: ensure within 4096
    if len(message) > 4096:
        # Drop trailers if needed
        # Find the blank line before trailers (we have already built it), replace trailers with CRLF
        message = b''.join(parts) + b"0" + last_ext + b"\r\n\r\n"
        if len(message) > 4096:
            # As a fallback, regenerate with a single small chunk and no trailers
            payload = _rand_ascii_bytes(rng, 8)
            message = b"8\r\n" + payload + b"\r\n0\r\n\r\n"

    return message
